title: Put ticfac in the orchestrator image
description:
The image already carries tk, git, Go, ripgrep and a real filesystem, and has /usr/local/bin/ticks-orchestrator as the role entrypoint the Run Workflow starts and streams. It does NOT carry ticfac - zero mentions in image/Dockerfile. That is the gap this epic turns on.

Add the ticfac binary the way everything else in that image is added: pinned and checksummed in the version block at the top, so a rebuild is a diff of that block. Note the image is 'pinned to the tk version it embeds' - ticfac's pin belongs beside it and moves with it.

Nothing else in this tick. Do not change the entrypoint yet.
notes:
2026-09-21 08:21 - HOW ticfac gets in, decided after reading the image and the deploy.

tk is installed with 'go install github.com/pengelbrecht/ticks/cmd/tk@<ref>' - built in the image from a module path, which is why Go is in the image. That does NOT work for ticfac: ticfac is a PRIVATE repository, so a build-time 'go install' would need credentials inside the Docker build.

Use the mechanism the deploy already has instead. The image context is //go:embed'ed in the ticfac binary and materialized to the staged dir by MaterializeSandbox, whose contract is already 'what Docker builds is exactly this binary's image'. So:

1. At deploy, cross-compile ticfac AND ticfac-exec-subprocess for linux, into the staged image context. The deploying machine has Go - it has just built ticfac.
2. The Dockerfile COPYs them onto PATH.

This gives a property the deploy already wants and states elsewhere: the orchestrator binary and the embedded bundle come from the EXACT SAME COMMIT, guaranteed, with no registry and no credentials in the build.

Architecture: the Dockerfile already carries *_SHA256_AMD64 and *_SHA256_ARM64 pins, so it is built for either. Stage both (ticfac-linux-amd64, ticfac-linux-arm64) and select with COPY ticfac-linux-, rather than guessing which platform the build will target. Verify TARGETARCH is available in this build path before relying on it.

Do NOT forget ticfac-exec-subprocess. The run refuses to start without it beside the binary, correctly - 'a run without it would start jobs nothing is watching' - and that refusal cost a restart cycle during the 2026-09-20 gate run.
2026-09-21 08:24 - CORRECTION to my earlier note, 2026-09-21. It said to add the pin to image/Dockerfile's version block. That is WRONG and would fail CI.

image/ is a VENDORED copy of pengelbrecht/ticks' cloud/sandbox tree, pinned by sandbox.pin.json, whose contract is 'ticfac never edits a file under image/'. The CI job  runs both 'go run ./cmd/sandbox check' (offline digests) and 'go run ./cmd/sandbox verify-upstream' (fetches ticks at the pinned ref and compares byte for byte). Any edit to the repo's copy fails.

Nor does the fix belong upstream in ticks: ticks' own build context has no ticfac binaries, so COPY lines there would break every ticks image build.

The right mechanism is the one the deploy already uses for the tk pins - SetSandboxTkPins rewrites the STAGED copy, never the repo copy. So:

1. deploy cross-compiles ticfac and ticfac-exec-subprocess for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 into the staged image context, after MaterializeSandbox (whose pruneStale removes the previous deploy's binaries first, so staleness cannot accumulate).
2. deploy rewrites the STAGED Dockerfile: ARG TICFAC_VERSION and ARG TICFAC_SHA256_AMD64/ARM64 into the version block, plus a checksummed COPY / sha256sum -c / chmod / 'ticfac version' block, TARGETARCH-selected.

Net effect inside the container is identical; the pin lives in the deployed Dockerfile rather than the vendored one. The image stays generic and the DEPLOY specialises it, which is the existing layering rather than a new one.

Found by the agent implementing this, by reading the vendoring contract before editing the file I pointed it at.
acceptance_criteria: ticfac is on PATH inside the orchestrator container with its version pinned and checksummed in image/Dockerfile's version block, and 'ticfac version' answers from inside a running container
closed_reason: Landed via PR #25. The deploy cross-compiles ticfac and ticfac-exec-subprocess for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 into the STAGED image context and rewrites the staged Dockerfile's pins - image/ is vendored from ticks and never edited here. Verified by building the real staged context and running the container: 'ticfac version' answers and ticfac-exec-subprocess is on PATH. +15.4 MB on a 2.95 GB image.
